prompt:
A densely annotated editorial infographic plate, drawn by hand in confident ink
line with light watercolour and gouache wash on bright warm-white paper.
Contour line varies in weight and is charcoal near-black. Dimensional but not
photographic: restrained hatching, subtle texture, believable volume, selective
shadow, clean uncluttered background. Every material reads as itself — dull grey
lead, unglazed earthenware, weathered timber, damp fibrous bark — and materials
that differ in the explanation look visibly different. Quiet palette of stone,
clay, wood, and metal tones over the warm-white ground, with one or two
desaturated accents that each keep a single meaning throughout the plate.
Contemporary editorial typography: one calm display face for the title, one
highly legible face for the many small labels, sentence case, crisply printed
and correctly spelled. Annotation is dense and disciplined — leader lines,
brackets, dimension marks, magnified inset circles, small side studies — laid
out so no two leaders cross. Asymmetric composition with about a quarter of the
page left quiet. Modern printing on clean stock: fresh, crisp, and unaged. The
only lettering anywhere on the plate is the title, the deck, the labels, and the
short notes. The words hero, drawing, figure, plate, inset, zone, band, strip,
trio, column, and cutaway describe the construction of the page and are never
lettered onto it, alone or in a phrase: no headings that name parts of the
layout, no percentages or
proportions of the page, no tags in brackets after a label or note, no sentence
describing the drawing or explaining what the reader is meant to see, no
signature, monogram, date, watermark, or credit line.

The plate is headed "read-annotations", with the standing line "Reads the notes an author left on a scanned book's pages and sorts them into rotate, no-sky, and chapter lists by page." beneath it.

The dominant picture, filling roughly half the page, shows An open annotated PDF of a scanned book, drawn as three fanned pages. The first page holds a picture printed sideways, with a note reading "rotate." The second holds a landscape photograph, with a note reading "no sky" near its top edge. The third is a chapter-opening page with a note reading "The Mill Race." The notes lift off the pages and travel rightward through a three-way sorting gate. Each note drops into one of three trays, and arrows run from the pages to the trays.

Magnified circles set beside it show circle one shows a note that matches only the single word rotate. Circle two shows a note that begins with "no sky" or "no_sky." Circle three shows any other wording falling through to become a chapter title. study one shows a blank note set aside. Study two shows notes ordered by page number, then by kind. Study three shows one printed line per note.

Colour is used so that Red marks rotate. Blue marks no sky. Ochre marks chapter titles.

Draw these quantities as dimension marks or counts: 3 kinds of note, drawn as three trays. 2 output formats, text and yaml. 3 lists in the yaml output. 2 sort keys, page then kind.

These trade words appear on the plate, each set against the thing it names: "annotated PDF" sits on the fanned pages. "rotate" sits on the sideways picture's note. "no sky" and "no_sky" sit on the landscape note and its circle. "chapter" sits on the chapter-opener note and the ochre tray. "--pdf" sits on the arrow feeding the PDF in. "--format yaml" sits on the yaml output. "rotations," "no_sky," and "chapters" sit on the three yaml lists. "manifest.yaml" sits on the destination file those lists paste into.

Letter these words onto the drawings, spelled exactly as given: annotated PDF, rotate, no sky, The Mill Race, page 41, sideways image, chapter opener exactly rotate, starts with no sky, or no_sky, everything else, case ignored blank notes skipped, sort by page, then by kind, one line each rotations, no_sky, chapters, title, manifest.yaml --pdf, --format yaml, text, yaml

Set these short notes beside what they explain: The author marks pages while paging through. Only the bare word rotate counts; Any other note becomes a chapter title. Empty notes are dropped before sorting. Lists shaped for pasting into the manifest; Chapters keep their title text. Plain text is the default output.
